subsystems.name: Abiotic pathway catalogue
subsystems.role: lists every known non-biological way to make a candidate gas, so a detection is never interpreted in isolation.

subsystems.name: Photochemical and climate models
subsystems.role: simulate the candidate planet's atmosphere to see whether the observed gases can coexist without life.

subsystems.name: Retrieval and instrument model
subsystems.role: turns a measured spectrum into gas abundances with honest error bars.

subsystems.name: Planetary context dataset
subsystems.role: supplies the star, orbit and environment that determine which explanations are plausible.

subsystems.name: Assessment logic
subsystems.role: the decision rules that convert model comparisons into a stated confidence level.

buildSteps.title: Characterise star and planet
buildSteps.detail: Measure the host star's brightness and ultraviolet output and the planet's mass, radius and orbit; these set which chemistry is possible.

buildSteps.title: Retrieve the spectrum
buildSteps.detail: Fit the observed transmission or emission spectrum to derive abundances of gases such as oxygen, methane, carbon dioxide and water, with uncertainties.

buildSteps.title: Enumerate abiotic sources
buildSteps.detail: Working through the catalogue, list every non-biological route to each detected gas — for example oxygen from water vapour broken apart by ultraviolet light followed by hydrogen escape.

buildSteps.title: Run the models
buildSteps.detail: Feed each plausible scenario into photochemical and climate models and check whether it reproduces the observation within the error bars.

buildSteps.title: Compare hypotheses
buildSteps.detail: Score or rank the biological and abiotic explanations against the same data rather than testing life alone.

buildSteps.title: Report the surviving gap
buildSteps.detail: State what remains unexplained after abiotic options are exhausted, with uncertainty, instead of presenting the raw detection as a life claim.

buildSteps.title: Set falsification tests
buildSteps.detail: Specify which follow-up observation — another gas, a different wavelength band, a time-variation — would break the preferred explanation.

buildSteps.title: Reassess as data improve
buildSteps.detail: Re-run the framework whenever better spectra, stellar data or new abiotic pathways appear, and revise the confidence accordingly.

prerequisites.why: water and carbon dioxide have been measured in hot giant planets since 2022, but thin atmospheres around small rocky worlds remain at the edge of capability.
codes tested against Venus, Earth and Titan underpin the abiotic baselines; extending them to unfamiliar planets is the weak point.
measured absorption line lists are needed to identify gases in a spectrum at all.
new non-biological pathways keep being identified, so any catalogue is provisional.

prerequisites.tech: Telescopes able to see several gases at once
prerequisites.why: a single gas means little; a confident assessment needs simultaneous detection of a combination that ordinary chemistry cannot sustain.

pathway.milestone: framework applied to solar-system planets, Archean Earth analogues and simulated exoplanet spectra, and used to interpret current telescope data
pathway.unlocks: discipline of publishing explanatory gaps rather than bare detections.

pathway.milestone: application to the first rocky-planet atmospheres resolved with current and under-construction telescopes
pathway.unlocks: real test cases, and pressure to standardise the scoring and uncertainty conventions.

pathway.milestone: reflected-light spectra of temperate Earth-sized planets from a dedicated direct-imaging space telescope
pathway.unlocks: multiple gases measured together, where the framework's hypothesis comparison becomes decisive.

pathway.milestone: observational networks that track seasonal and long-term variability, plus agnostic signatures for unfamiliar biochemistry
pathway.unlocks: biosignature claims that rest on repeated, independent lines of evidence rather than one spectrum.
